nodes.title: What Is Technology?
nodes.summary: Technology is a means to do something faster, cheaper, stronger, safer, or more effectively; AI belongs in a continuum from the wheel and printing press to modern automation.

nodes.title: AI Is Not the Problem
nodes.summary: AI is not inherently evil; purpose, proportion, sequencing, and downstream consequences matter.

nodes.title: Paradox of Automation
nodes.summary: Individually rational automation can become collectively destructive when labor-income elimination undermines aggregate demand and firms' own markets.

nodes.title: Missing First Rung
nodes.summary: Reduced hiring of entry-level workers can damage the labor pipeline even before mass layoffs appear.

nodes.title: Cognitive vs Physical Automation
nodes.summary: Information jobs are easier to automate first; dexterous, site-specific physical work requires more engineering and generally comes later.

nodes.title: 100-Person Island
nodes.summary: One robot owner replaces 99 workers. Productive capacity explodes while purchasing power disappears.

nodes.title: Valley Before Abundance
nodes.summary: Even if AI eventually creates abundance, the transition may include unemployment, demand collapse, asset stress, unrest, and political instability.

nodes.title: Money, Scarcity & Allocation
nodes.summary: Zero economic profit is not zero price. Scarce goods still require an allocation mechanism.

nodes.title: Nature, Overshoot & Equilibrium
nodes.summary: Nature rebalances overshoot ruthlessly; AI/economic systems may self-correct similarly unless humans design gentler feedback mechanisms.

nodes.title: Ethical AI Transition
nodes.summary: Fairness, speed, warning, support, and sequencing matter. Progress should not ambush people who have no realistic time to adapt.

nodes.title: AI Layoffs & Hiring Evidence
nodes.summary: Track layoffs, reduced hiring, entry-level exposure, occupation changes, and employer disclosures tied to AI.

nodes.title: Autonomous Robotics
nodes.summary: Track controlled-environment robotics first, then less structured physical work.

nodes.title: Automation of Danger vs Livelihood
nodes.summary: Automating danger can protect humans; automating livelihoods changes the income-and-demand system.

nodes.title: Paradox of Thrift Analogy
nodes.summary: What is rational for one actor can be destructive when everyone does it.

nodes.title: Race to Automate / Tragedy of Commons
nodes.summary: Firms may automate because competitors will; no conspiracy is required for collectively destructive outcomes.

nodes.title: Expertise Pipeline Problem
nodes.summary: If junior roles disappear, future senior professionals may never accumulate the experience organizations still need.

nodes.title: Controlled Environments First
nodes.summary: Physical automation can arrive sooner when environments are constrained or redesigned around machines.

nodes.title: Claim on Production
nodes.summary: If labor no longer determines income, what gives humans a legitimate claim on machine-produced goods and services?

nodes.title: Social Instability / Revolution Risk
nodes.summary: Rapid unemployment, inequality, and collapsing expectations can create unrest or revolutionary pressure.

nodes.title: Abundance Is Not Infinite Supply
nodes.summary: Land, energy, materials, desirable locations, time, and unique experiences remain scarce even in high-productivity worlds.

nodes.title: Mouse Plague Analogy
nodes.summary: Population/resource overshoot illustrates brutal self-correction when feedback is ignored.

nodes.title: Speed & Fairness
nodes.summary: AI disruption can blindside ordinary people before they understand what is happening or have time to retrain.

nodes.title: Gold Rush / Tulip Bubble Analogy
nodes.summary: Competitive frenzy and fear of missing extraordinary returns can drive capital and behavior to extremes.

nodes.title: Oil Extraction Race
nodes.summary: Individually rational extraction can create collective oversupply; used as an analogy for automation races.

nodes.title: Luddite / Industrial Transition History
nodes.summary: Mechanization, worker resistance, state suppression, and long transition periods provide a contrast with today's faster AI disruption.

nodes.title: Musk No-Money / Abundance Thesis
nodes.summary: Examine claims that AI makes work optional and money irrelevant; distinguish abundance from scarcity and zero economic profit from zero price.

nodes.title: Fossil Fuel Transition Comparison
nodes.summary: Fossil fuels had decades of warning and still have not fully transitioned; AI gives workers far less runway.

nodes.title: Capitalism Has No Brake Pedal
nodes.summary: Competitive capitalism rewards short-term cost reduction and market capture even when collective adoption may destabilize demand.

nodes.title: Government Capture / Follow the Money
nodes.summary: Lobbying, subsidies, pay-to-play incentives, short-term politics, and weak foresight can obstruct transition planning.

nodes.title: Government Failure / Need for Collective Adoption
nodes.summary: One ethical firm cannot stabilize the economy alone; systemic problems require collective rules or shared mechanisms.

nodes.title: Weak UBI Critique
nodes.summary: Very low UBI levels such as $10k-$12k/year cannot support modern housing, healthcare, education, retirement, and middle-class consumption.

nodes.title: Post-Work Meaning & Identity
nodes.summary: Work provides income, structure, identity, contribution, and purpose; mass displacement can create a meaning crisis.

nodes.title: AI Safety vs Economic Safety
nodes.summary: Traditional AI safety focuses on misuse/alignment; economic destabilization from job destruction deserves comparable attention.

nodes.title: Autonomous Warfare
nodes.summary: AI in warfare and life-and-death decision systems is a distinct nefarious use requiring strong ethical limits.

nodes.title: Lifespan Extension & System Design
nodes.summary: Longer lifespans can stress pension, Social Security, healthcare, and retirement assumptions.

nodes.title: Prevention vs Lifespan Extension
nodes.summary: Preventing early death differs systemically from broadly extending lifespan.

nodes.title: Ethical Use Cases for AI
nodes.summary: Use AI for materials, recycling, climate, dangerous environments, firefighting, nuclear accidents, and pandemic prevention.

nodes.title: Economic Profit Tends Toward Zero
nodes.summary: Competitive markets tend to erode supernormal economic profits; this does not imply zero prices or zero production costs.

nodes.title: Capital-Labor-IP Triangle
nodes.summary: AI may substitute for labor and portions of IP/knowledge, concentrating power in capital owners.

nodes.title: Production Without Consumption
nodes.summary: High productive capacity with insufficient labor income creates goods without enough purchasing power to consume them.

nodes.title: AI/Automation Dividend or Income Continuity
nodes.summary: Preserve purchasing power when machines replace labor; must be framed as system stabilization rather than a trivial handout.

nodes.title: Managed Transition / Work Reduction
nodes.summary: Use productivity gains to reduce hours rather than abruptly eliminate people.

nodes.title: AI Impact / Systems Consequence Assessment
nodes.summary: Assess labor, demand, retirement, housing, tax-base, and social-stability effects before large-scale deployment.
